instruction.what: The evidence validation (B5) of one subgroup, after its sweep, the gate before 3.1: the code checks of its observations (shown in `code_checks`), and the reading of every evidence observation of the subgroup (its own of S1 to 2.1, and the older ones on its occurrences kept as evidence) for whether it is true, founded and coherent with the others. Inner being is not judged here; the two validations are never run together.
read: Read the code checks first: a failing check names observations to repair (unmarked, no node, a word node missing a column without its reason, a trace to a deleted observation, two of one text, a B1 observation no sense traces, a sense the 2.1 observations on its occurrences do not trace, an older observation left open).

Take one observation at a time (`observations`, in the order of the steps): its text, basis and grounds against its verses (`verses`) and the observations it traces. Is it true of those verses? Does it say more than they show? Does it contradict another observation of the subgroup?
write: Fill `answer.observations`, one entry for each observation of the package: verdict true, with `why` (what in the verses and the data bears it out); or verdict repair, with `why` (what is wrong) and `actions`: the actions of the validation that repair it (cfg_setting validate.reading actions, each with its parameters, for example {"action": "restate", "oid": id, "new_text": ..., "checked": ..., "reason": ...}, or delete_neither, complete_node, add_trace).
A repair is checked as it is written; an observation that cannot be made true is deleted with its reason.

Then: Collection-Build.ps1 -Action RecordEvidence -File <the answer file> (-Check to preview), and ReadEvidence again until every evidence observation is read; the gate passes when all are read and the code checks pass.

keep.text: A sheet of validation actions is checked whole (every action named, its parameters complete) and written in one transaction: any action the tables refuse refuses the whole sheet and nothing is kept. -Check runs every action and rolls back. Every change is kept in ib_observation_change with its reason (RW-01); nothing is physically deleted.

A finding of the validation is repaired first: a wording that is untrue or stronger than its verse is restated and the restatement checked against the base data; a node missing a column is completed, or the reason the data cannot give it is recorded; a duplicate is consolidated; a node is deleted only when another live node carries its occurrence or it supports no finding of its observation. A finding is left open only when a named collection's validation will touch the observation: the deferral to that collection and the finding are recorded, and the check accepts it as deferred. A finding with no named owner is closed in the validation.

An older observation is deleted as consumed only when live observations carry its meaning: every word occurrence of it is on a live node of a carrier or named as not carried with its reason, the mapping is stated in words (what the old says, which carrier states each part), the traces to it are re-pointed or replaced, and the consumption is kept as `consumed_by`. An observation that holds more than one finding is split first.

An observation that is neither evidence nor inner being contributes nothing to the purposes of the observations (researcher, 2026-11-22): it is commented with its reason and the word occurrences no other live observation holds, then deleted. An observation already marked, or one another observation traces, is not deleted this way.

Evidence states what the data are or show, tied to a verse. Inner being states how something works in the inner being, based on evidence, a building block of the stage 5 claims. The marker (ib_observation.nature) follows the content and purpose of the observation, never its stage (RS-04): an observation of any stage may be inner being when it traces to evidence. One that states both is split. The marker is set when the observation is created, by the item that is answered (cfg_setting layer.reading items.<item>.nature); a finding file never sets it; the validation changes it only where the content shows the item's nature does not hold.

The validation runs in two layers, never concurrently: evidence first, then inner being. The inner-being layer is judged only when the evidence layer passes (every in-scope observation marked, none without a live node, no word node missing a required column without its reason, no live trace to a deleted observation, no two of one meaning). A later evidence change reopens only the inner-being rows it touches. In the build this gate is: step 3.1 does not open before the evidence layer passes, and step 3.3 does not close before both layers pass (cfg_setting layer.reading open_gate and closing_gate).
No observation is changed except by a reading, and every change is recorded with its reason. An observation no longer supported by the verse is soft-deleted, with the reason.
One observation per finding: the same description is never written twice. Applied to another verse, word or scope it gains a node on the existing observation.
Observation text is concise and tied to this verse's content, never a restatement of the word's dictionary sense. A transliteration is never given without its gloss.
Verse references are resolved fresh at write time, never taken from the text written. Relations are recorded only on evidence.
Missing data in the base extract is named as a gap, never substituted from memory or outside knowledge.

observations.text: In Mar 10:42 'considered' is said of those who are thought to be rulers of the Gentiles: it is their standing as seen by others, what they are held to be, not an act of the one who thinks.
observations.grounds: those who are considered rulers

observations.text: In Mat 1:20 'considered' is Joseph turning over in his mind what he had resolved about Mary, the point at which the angel appears to him.
observations.grounds: as he considered these things

observations.text: In Heb 11:11 and Heb 11:26 'considered' is a reckoned judgment: Sarah judges the one who promised to be faithful, and Moses counts the reproach of Christ greater wealth than Egypt's treasures. It is a conclusion reached, with the thing weighed named in each verse.
observations.grounds: she considered him faithful

observations.text: In Rom 4:19 'considered' is Abraham fixing his attention on his own body and on the barrenness of Sarah's womb, the facts he looked at without his faith weakening.
observations.grounds: when he considered his own body

observations.text: In Heb 11:19 'considered' is a reckoned conclusion: Abraham reasons that God can raise the dead, and the verse says he received Isaac back in that figure.
observations.grounds: He considered that God was able

observations.text: In Rom 4:19 this code is the Greek negative particle that the English folds into 'did not weaken in faith when he considered'. It carries no sense of considering; the consideration is the verb of G2657 in the same verse.
observations.grounds: He did not weaken in faith

observations.text: In Dan 7:8 'considered' is the seer's close watching of the horns as another comes up among them: an attentive look at what he sees in the vision, told in the first person.
observations.grounds: I considered the horns

observations.text: In 1Ki 10:21, 2Ch 9:20 and Neh 13:13 'considered' is counted as: silver is counted as nothing in Solomon's days, and the men appointed over the storehouses are counted reliable. It is a valuation, an account made of a thing or a person.
observations.grounds: silver was not considered as anything

observations.text: In Pro 17:28 'considered' is being counted as wise: the fool who holds his tongue is taken by others to be wise. It is how a person is reckoned by observers, not what he thinks.
observations.grounds: is considered wise

observations.text: In Job 1:8, Job 2:3 and Pro 24:32 the Hebrew behind 'considered' is the word for heart in a phrase of setting the heart on something: the Lord asks Satan whether he has fixed his heart on Job, and the observer in Proverbs sets his heart on the field and takes instruction. It is giving thought, with the heart as its place.
observations.grounds: Have you considered my servant Job

observations.text: In Ecc 2:11 'considered' is the Preacher turning to look over all his hands had done and the toil spent: a survey of his works that ends in the verdict that all was vanity.
observations.grounds: Then I considered all that my hands

observations.text: In Eze 18:28 'considered' is the sinner seeing his transgressions and turning from them; the seeing is the step before the turning and the verse says he will live because of it.
observations.grounds: Because he considered and turned away

observations.text: In Job 1:8 and Job 2:3 'considered' is the verb of setting, in the phrase of setting the heart on Job: the Lord asks whether Satan has fixed attention on his servant.
observations.grounds: Have you considered my servant Job

observations.text: In Isa 53:8 'considered' is the generation of the servant giving thought to his being cut off: the question asks who among them took it to heart or gave it a thought.
observations.grounds: who considered that he was cut off

observations.text: In Pro 24:32 'considered' is the observer setting his heart on what he has seen, the verb of setting with the heart as its object, after which he takes instruction.
observations.grounds: I saw and considered it

observations.text: In Dan 7:8 'considered' (Aramaic) is the seer contemplating the horns, the intent looking at what he sees; the same scene as the other code, in the one verse.
observations.grounds: I considered the horns

observations.text: In Luk 22:24 'regarded' is being accounted the greatest: the dispute among the disciples is over who is to be held of highest standing.
observations.grounds: to be regarded as the greatest

observations.text: In Rom 2:26 and Rom 8:36 'regarded' is being counted as something: the uncircumcised keeping the law is counted as circumcision, and the believers are counted as sheep for slaughter.
observations.grounds: will not his uncircumcision be regarded

observations.text: In Gen 31:15, Psa 44:22, Lam 4:2 and Hos 8:12 'regarded' is being counted as: as foreigners, as sheep to be slaughtered, as earthen pots, and the laws as a strange thing. It is how someone or something is reckoned by another.
observations.grounds: we are regarded as sheep

observations.text: In Isa 29:16 and Isa 29:17 'regarded' is being counted as: the potter as if he were clay, and the field as if it were a forest. It is a reckoning set against the order of things.
observations.grounds: Shall the potter be regarded as the clay

observations.text: In 2Cor 5:16 'regard' is knowing or taking account of a person in some way: Paul says that from now on he takes account of no one according to the flesh, even of Christ, as once he did.
observations.grounds: we regard no one according to the flesh

observations.text: In 2Th 3:15 and 1Ti 6:1 'regard' is counting someone as something: the brother who is warned is not counted an enemy, and masters are counted worthy of honor by the servants.
observations.grounds: Do not regard him as an enemy

observations.text: In 1Co 4:1 and 1Pe 5:12 'regard' is counting someone as something: servants of Christ and stewards, and Silvanus as a faithful brother in the writer's judgment.
observations.grounds: one should regard us

observations.text: In Col 2:16 'regard' is part of the phrase 'with regard to': it marks the matter in respect of which no one is to judge, a festival, a new moon or a Sabbath. It carries no sense of thinking.
observations.grounds: with regard to a festival

observations.text: In 2Cor 5:16 this code is the Greek verb of knowing in the perfect, 'we have known' Christ according to the flesh; it is the counting or taking account of him that Paul says he now gives up.
observations.grounds: we once regarded Christ according to

observations.text: In Exo 5:9 this code is the Hebrew negative particle in the phrase 'pay no regard': it carries the 'no' of the command and not the sense of regarding, which the verb of H8159 in the same verse carries.
observations.grounds: pay no regard to lying words

observations.text: In Psa 28:5 'regard' is discerning or attending to the works of the Lord and the work of his hands; the verse says those who do not regard them will be torn down.
observations.grounds: they do not regard the works of the Lord

observations.text: In Ecc 3:18 'with regard to' is a Hebrew noun of matter or cause in the phrase 'concerning the children of man'; it marks what the saying is about and carries no thinking of its own.
observations.grounds: with regard to the children of man

observations.text: In Isa 13:17 and Isa 33:8 'regard' is valuing or counting: the Medes put no value on silver, and in the ruined land there is no account taken of man.
observations.grounds: no regard for silver

observations.text: In Job 9:21, Psa 144:3 and Pro 12:10 'regard' is knowing and taking notice with care: Job says he does not take notice of himself, the psalmist asks what man is that God takes notice of him, and the righteous man knows and cares for his beast's life.
observations.grounds: that you regard him

observations.text: In Job 9:21 this code is the Hebrew negative particle of 'I regard not myself'; it carries the 'not', and the verb of H3045 carries the regarding.
observations.grounds: I regard not myself

observations.text: In 1Sa 25:25 'regard' is the heart in the phrase of setting the heart on something: Abigail asks that her lord not give his heart to the worthless Nabal, that is, not take him to heart.
observations.grounds: Let not my lord regard this worthless fellow

observations.text: In Psa 74:20, Isa 5:12 and Lam 4:16 'regard' is looking at and paying attention: asking God to look to the covenant, the feasters not looking on the Lord's deeds, and the Lord no longer looking on the priests with favor.
observations.grounds: they do not regard the deeds of the Lord

observations.text: In Jer 24:5 'regard as good' is recognizing and acknowledging: the Lord says he will look on the good figs, the exiles, as good, taking them as such.
observations.grounds: so I will regard as good the exiles

observations.text: In 2Ki 3:14 'have regard for' is the idiom of lifting the face: Elisha says it is only for Jehoshaphat's sake, out of respect for him, that he attends to the king of Israel.
observations.grounds: I have regard for Jehoshaphat the king

observations.text: In 1Sa 1:16 'regard as' is the verb of setting or putting: Hannah asks Eli not to set her down as a worthless woman, that is, not to take her for one.
observations.grounds: Do not regard your servant as a worthless woman

observations.text: In Lev 19:23 'regard as' is the verb of treating a fruit as uncircumcised: the tree's fruit is to be counted forbidden for three years and not eaten.
observations.grounds: you shall regard its fruit as forbidden

observations.text: In Deu 9:27 and 2Ch 6:19 'regard' is the verb of turning toward: Moses asks God not to turn to the people's stubbornness, and Solomon asks him to turn to the prayer of his servant. It is where the attention is directed.
observations.grounds: Do not regard the stubbornness of this people

observations.text: In Psa 80:14 'have regard for' is the verb of visiting and attending to: the psalmist asks God to look down and attend to the vine, in a prayer to turn again.
observations.grounds: have regard for this vine

observations.text: In Deu 33:9 and Job 37:24 'regard' is the verb of seeing: Levi did not look on his father and mother in a way that favored them, and God does not look on those who are wise in their own conceit. The sense is giving notice, or refusing it.
observations.grounds: he does not regard any who are wise
